examples.japanese: {腕時計|うでどけい}を{見|み}て{時間|じかん}を{確認|かくにん}した。
examples.english: I checked the time on my wristwatch.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}から{腕時計|うでどけい}をもらった。
examples.english: I received a wristwatch from my father.

examples.japanese: この{腕時計|うでどけい}は{防水|ぼうすい}{機能|きのう}がついている。
examples.english: This wristwatch has a waterproof function.

examples.japanese: {卒業|そつぎょう}のお{祝|いわ}いに{腕時計|うでどけい}を{買|か}ってもらった。
examples.english: I had a wristwatch bought for me as a graduation gift.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}はスマホで{時間|じかん}を{見|み}る{人|ひと}が{多|おお}いが、{腕時計|うでどけい}をしている{人|ひと}もまだたくさんいる。
examples.english: Recently many people check the time on their smartphones, but there are still many people who wear wristwatches.

notes:
{腕時計|うでどけい} is a compound of {腕|うで} (arm/wrist) and {時計|とけい} (clock/watch). It refers specifically to a watch worn on the wrist.

Common types:
- アナログ{腕時計|うでどけい} (analog watch)
- デジタル{腕時計|うでどけい} (digital watch)
- スマートウォッチ (smartwatch)

Related terms:
- {時計|とけい} (clock, watch - general)
- {懐中時計|かいちゅうどけい} (pocket watch)
- {置|お}き{時計|どけい} (table clock)

Note: With smartphones, fewer young people wear {腕時計|うでどけい}, though they remain popular as accessories and status symbols.
